A user returned an iPad Pro months earlier because there was no good ssh/mosh client and found Panic's Prompt awkward. Blink makes them consider trying the iPad again as a portable terminal.
The US$19.99 price is a bit steep to buy sight-unseen, which the user calls more an App Store problem than Blink's fault. The price is fine if it works better than Prompt.
I bought it after the discussion here. I'm super impressed.
Been using it (beta testing on iPhone and paid version on iPad so I can compare) for a while. Improving steadily, solid connectivity. So far happy with it, even if the price felt somewhat high.

Bought it even though it apparently has no agent forwarding. Pretty good, refresh seems faster than Prompt, especially when using htop and tmux on the LAN (something that always bugged me about Prompt). The user still wants mouse support and external display support.
A user asks for config sync via iCloud/Dropbox: "It's quite a pain to sync host lists across several iOS devices."
A user wants 1Password import of private keys and Citrix X1 mouse support, noting that terminals are more useful with mice too.

A beta tester praises the excellent design, highly accurate and fast rendering, and mosh support. They say the open source process blows competitors like Prompt out of the water: the developer, Carlos, is highly responsive to feature requests and bug reports on GitHub, so users feel they have real influence over features.

One user is personally fine with the $20 price but thinks it is steep for casual users and may hinder adoption. They note you can compile it yourself for free and say they would happily donate around $5/month for continued development.
